Geodesic Dome - 2V subdivided icosahedron

Build a 2V (frequency-2) geodesic sphere of radius `R = 3.0 m`, centered at the world origin. No initial file is provided; construct the mesh from scratch.

Construction rule:
1. Start from a regular icosahedron inscribed in a sphere of radius `R`. Use the canonical golden-ratio vertices (+/-1, +/-phi, 0) and permutations, then scale each vertex so its distance from origin equals `R`.
2. For each of the 20 triangular faces, connect the midpoints of its 3 edges to produce 4 sub-triangles (1 inverted central triangle + 3 corner triangles).
3. Project every new midpoint vertex onto the sphere of radius `R` as well (normalize the vector then multiply by `R`). Shared edges between neighboring original faces must reuse the same midpoint vertex (no vertex duplication).

Export the result as a single OBJ file.

Save the native SketchUp model to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp`.

Requirements:
1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp` can be opened and inspected as a native SketchUp model.
2. Vertex count is exactly 42 (12 original icosahedron + 30 unique edge midpoints).
3. Face count is exactly 80 triangles (20 icosahedron faces x 4).
4. Every vertex lies on the sphere of radius 3 m within 0.5 mm.
5. All faces are triangles.
6. The mesh is a closed manifold (every edge shared by exactly 2 faces).
7. The set of edge lengths resolves into exactly 2 distinct length classes (2V geodesic has two strut types - apex-to-midpoint and midpoint-to-midpoint).
source: Buckminster Fuller geodesic subdivision (public domain); SU-Ruby `entities.add_face`; Wavefront OBJ specification
